calc.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
calc.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg OPEN QUESTION (2026-07): native engineer corrected 'дебит' to 'водно количество' in hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings (rc_, or_). Whether to replace 'дебит' suite-wide (incl. pipes/irrigation) is pending their clarification; keep 'дебит' elsewhere until answered.

calc.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
calc.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

calc.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators.
calc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term.

ip.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
ip.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred.

ip.context: A drip irrigation emitter (dripper/micro-sprinkler) that delivers water at a controlled low flow rate directly to the soil or plant root zone. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the field term most familiar to irrigation practitioners in the target language. Arabic: 'قطارة' (dripper) is the field term, preferred over the academic 'مُصدِر'. Spanish: 'gotero' is field-common in Latin America alongside the technical 'emisor'. Ukrainian: 'крапельниця' is the field term used by irrigation workers.

ip.context: Ratio of minimum to average emitter flow rate in a drip or sprinkler system. DU = q_min / q_avg. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the irrigation engineering standard term. 'Uniformity' refers to how evenly water is distributed across the field, not physical evenness of the system. When the source says 'low-quarter DU', see the separate 'low-quarter distribution uniformity' entry. Hebrew: אחידות — never the nonword הוודות (found in shipped he file).

ip.context: Irrigation statistic: average of the lowest quarter of measured emitter flows divided by the overall average. Referenced in Irrigation Pressure notes as "textbook low-quarter Distribution Uniformity".
ip.translation_notes: Use the established irrigation-engineering phrase; do not invent one. "Textbook" is an adjective meaning "as defined in standard textbooks" — fr rendered it "manuel" (manual check), wrong. he: uniformity = אחידות, never the nonword הוודות.
ip.preferred_translation: uniformité de distribution du quart inférieur

ip.context: Depth of water applied per unit time by a drip or sprinkler system. PR = q / A_e. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: In irrigation, 'application rate' or 'precipitation rate' (for sprinklers) or 'irrigation rate'. Use the field irrigation term. Do not use a water-quality or chemical-application connotation.

ip.context: Irrigation branch line carrying emitters, fed by the mainline. Pairs with "mainline". Appears throughout Irrigation Pressure.
ip.translation_notes: Branch pipe of a drip/sprinkler system — NOT the adjective "side/lateral". Wrong renderings found: sw "taji" (crown). fr irrigation standard is "rampe". Keep one word per language and never alternate (it file mixed "laterale" and "manichetta").

ip.context: The trunk/supply pipe feeding the laterals in an irrigation system. Pairs with "lateral".
ip.translation_notes: Translate "main/mainline" as the trunk pipe, not the adjective "main". fr file left "main" untranslated ("Tronçons Main") — wrong.

ip.context: A segment of pipe or channel between two nodes/cross-sections. Table rows in Irrigation Pressure are reaches.
ip.translation_notes: Hydraulics noun, NOT "arrival/reaching" (ps "رسیدل" wrong), NOT "agent" (sw "mwakala" wrong), NOT "stripe" (km wrong).

ip.context: Kinetic energy per unit weight, V²/2g — a height of water column.
ip.translation_notes: "Head" is a height of water column, never anatomical (cs "rychlostní hlava" wrong — use "rychlostní výška").

ip.context: Head loss along the pipe due to wall friction (Darcy-Weisbach). Irrigation Pressure table column.
Local head loss at fittings/valves/couplers (K_m coefficient). Irrigation Pressure table column.
The total-head line (elevation + pressure head + velocity head) along a pipe or channel. Appears in Irrigation Pressure Method note.
ip.translation_notes: Use the established hydraulics term for the total-head line. NEVER calque word-by-word: es "Linea de Grado de Energia", fr "ligne d'energie grade", it "Linea di Grado Energia", ro "Linia Gradului Energetic", bg/uk "line of the energy class", cs "energy layer" are all wrong renderings found in shipped files.
Hydraulics direction, never software "upgrade" (my file error). tr: memba = upstream, mansap = downstream — a tr file flipped these; pin them.

ip.context: Direction away from the supply, toward the outlet / last emitter.
ip.translation_notes: Never software "downgrade". ar: downstream = المصب / أسفل المجرى (a file used المنبعية = source-side, wrong).

mhp.context: Pressure pipe carrying water from a reservoir or headpond down to a turbine in a micro-hydro system. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Penstock' is a specialized term with no exact one-word equivalent in many languages. Use the established civil/hydro engineering phrase for 'pressure conduit' or 'force main to turbine'. Czech: 'tlakovod' (pressure main) is preferred over the generic 'přiváděcí potrubí' (supply pipe). Serbian: 'напорни цевовод' is the standard hydraulic engineering term.

mhp.context: Total elevation difference between the headpond water surface and the turbine — before subtracting penstock losses. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Gross' means total/before-deduction. Pair with 'net head' for clarity. Use the hydro-power standard term.

mhp.context: Effective head available at the turbine after subtracting penstock friction and minor losses from gross head. H_net = H_gross - h_L.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Net' means after-deduction. Pair with 'gross head'. Use the hydro-power standard term. WMO No. 385 entry 111 ('available head') gives the Russian term 'полезный напор' (useful head) / syn. 'располагаемый напор' — these overlap with net head in Russian hydro engineering practice.

mhp.context: Overall efficiency of a micro-hydro power plant — product of turbine, generator, and transmission efficiencies. Dimensionless, 0–1. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Plant' here means the power plant/installation, not a living plant. Use the energy/electrical engineering term for overall system efficiency.

mhp.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred.

mhp.context: A hydropower configuration that uses natural river flow without a dam or significant storage reservoir. Power output varies with seasonal river flow. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: Use the established energy/hydropower sector term. 'Run' means natural river current — do not translate as jogging or running. WMO No. 385 entry 1263 gives the full facility names: Spanish 'central hidroeléctrica de pasada', French 'usine hydroélectrique au fil de l'eau', Russian 'русловая гидроэлектростанция' — these are the authoritative terms for the power plant noun. The abbreviated forms 'filo de agua' (es), 'au fil de l'eau' (fr), and 'русловая ГЭС' (ru) are standard in engineering use. German: 'Laufwasserkraftwerk'. Chinese: '径流式水电'.

mhp.context: The intake structure at the upstream end of a penstock or canal, where water is diverted from the river or reservoir into the conveyance system. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator (penstock diameter and length descriptions).
mhp.translation_notes: Use the civil/irrigation engineering term for a water intake or diversion structure. Spanish: 'obra de toma'. French: 'ouvrage de prise d'eau'. Russian: 'водозаборное сооружение'. German: 'Einlaufbauwerk'. In many languages, 'intake structure' is preferred over a literal translation of 'headworks'.

mhp.context: Energy loss at pipe junctions, bends, fittings, and entrance — a local (point) loss as opposed to distributed friction loss along the pipe. H_m = k × v²/(2g). Also called 'minor loss', though in short penstocks these can equal or exceed friction losses. Appears in Manning Pipe Head Loss and Micro-Hydro Power calculators.
mhp.translation_notes: The term 'minor loss' is conventional but misleading — do not imply these losses are always small. Use the hydraulic engineering term for local/point losses at fittings. French: 'perte singulière'. Spanish: 'pérdida local' or 'pérdida por accesorio'. Russian: 'местные потери'. Chinese: '局部水头损失'.

mi.context: Cross-sectional flow area divided by wetted perimeter. Appears in Manning calculators.
mi.translation_notes: Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used the Latin loanword 'hidraulički radijus' — this form is widely used in South Slavic engineering practice and may be more recognizable to field practitioners than the native Slavic equivalents 'полупречник' (sr) / 'polumjer' (hr). Both are correct; native Slavic engineers may encounter both forms.

mi.context: Length of the channel or pipe boundary in contact with flowing water. Appears in Manning calculators.
mi.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1682 confirms: es = 'perímetro mojado', fr = 'périmètre mouillé'. Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. 'Wetted' here means 'in contact with water', not 'soaked'. Pre-2026 sr human used 'okvašeni obim' (obim = natural South Slavic word for perimeter/circumference); current uses 'квашени периметар' (периметар = Greek-derived loanword). Both are correct; 'obim/opseg' is more natural in informal Serbian/Croatian field use.

mi.context: Manning's n — empirical roughness coefficient used in the Manning formula for open-channel and pipe flow.
mi.translation_notes: Always include 'Manning' as a proper noun. The coefficient itself (n) needs no translation — only the label does. Do not translate as generic 'roughness coefficient' without 'Manning'.

mi.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators.

In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term.

mi.context: A channel whose cross-section is non-uniform / non-prismatic — a natural or surveyed section defined by station-elevation points, as opposed to a regular trapezoidal shape. Titles the Manning Irregular Channel calculator (mi_) and, in the geometric sense, the Weir Flow Irregular calculator (wi_).
mi.translation_notes: "Irregular" here is GEOMETRIC: the cross-section is non-uniform / natural / arbitrary shape. It is NOT the temporal sense "sporadic / occasional / not-regular" (bg "нередовен" WRONG, uk "нерегулярний" WRONG per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md), and NOT "incorrect / faulty" (ru "неправильное русло" reads as "wrong channel" — prefer "произвольного сечения"). Where the language allows, name the cross-section explicitly ("of irregular cross-section") rather than a bare adjective that could be read as temporal or evaluative.

ws.context: A flow-measurement or water-control structure — a barrier across a channel over which water flows. Appears in Weir Flow Simple and Weir Flow Irregular calculators.
ws.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1665 confirms: es = 'vertedero', fr = 'déversoir', ru = 'водослив'. In an irrigation context, the term often overlaps with 'diversion dam' or 'check structure'. Use the term most common among irrigation field workers in the target language, not a purely civil-engineering dictionary term.

ws.context: Water surface elevation on the upstream side of a weir or orifice. Appears in Weir Flow and Orifice calculators.
ws.translation_notes: 'Headwater' is an upstream water surface — do not confuse with 'head' (energy) or 'source' (origin of a stream). Use the hydraulic structure term.

ws.context: Water surface elevation on the downstream side of a weir or orifice. Appears in Orifice Flow calculator. When tailwater is above the invert, the orifice is submerged.
ws.translation_notes: Use the hydraulic structure term for downstream water level. Pair consistently with 'headwater elevation'.

ws.context: Coefficient correcting theoretical orifice or weir flow for real-world contraction and friction effects. Appears in Orifice and Weir calculators.
ws.translation_notes: The 'discharge' here refers to flow rate, not the verb. Use the hydraulic engineering compound term.

previous_translated.value: Chaque rangée est un tronçon le long du seul cheminement hydrauliquement au pire cas (cheminement de test) de l'alimentation au dernier goutteur. Un tronçon Main ne transmet le débit qu'aux rampes ne faisant pas partie du cheminement de test, donc son prélèvement est une multiplication plate (débit de conception × compte total de goutteur du tronçon) – pas de sensibilité de pression locale. La main est une conduite-mère partagée, donc le tronçon au point de prise de la rampe de test elle-même doit inclure non seulement les rampes entre ses propres extrémités mais aussi les rampes encore plus bas le long de la main au-delà de cette prise, ou partageant la même jonction (par exemple, une rampe de l'autre côté) – leur débit se divise à partir de ce même tronçon avant de se diviser, qu'elles apparaissent ou non ailleurs dans ce tableau. Un tronçon Rampe est un segment de la rampe de test elle-même : le débit du goutteur est calculé à partir de la pression locale réelle via q = k·H<sup>x</sup>, et la perte par friction est réduite par le facteur F(n) de Christiansen pour tenir compte du débit diminuant à mesure que chaque goutteur du tronçon prélève.
previous_translated.english: Each row is one reach along the single hydraulically worst path (the test path) from the supply to the last emitter. A Main reach only passes flow to laterals not on the test path, so its draw is a flat multiplication (design flow × the reach’s total emitter count) — no local pressure sensitivity. The main is a shared trunk pipe, so the reach right at the test lateral’s own takeoff must include not just laterals between its own endpoints but also any laterals still further down the main beyond that takeoff, or sharing the same junction (e.g. an opposite-side lateral) — their flow travels through that same reach before splitting off, whether or not they appear anywhere else in this table. A Lateral reach is a segment of the test lateral itself: emitter discharge is computed from the actual local pressure via q = k·H<sup>x</sup>, and friction loss is reduced by Christiansen’s F(n) factor to account for flow stepping down as each emitter in the reach draws off.

next_translated.value: Modélise une pression d'admission fixe (pas de courbe de pompe), un seul cheminement de test (pas le champ complet), et une courbe de goutteur à 2 paramètres (réglez l'exposant près de 0 pour approximer un goutteur auto-régulant). Deux ratios différents sont rapportés, délibérément séparés : q<sub>dernier</sub>/q<sub>moy,terrain</sub> est un contrôle d'uniformité, de forme similaire au contrôle manuel d'uniformité de distribution de bas quartile (moyenne du groupe bas ÷ moyenne de la population) mais calculé à partir des goutteurs modélisés de la rampe de test elle-même, corrigé par une estimation Δpression saisie plutôt qu'un échantillon statistique complet sur le terrain – la rampe de test est délibérément le pire cas présumé, sa moyenne brute non corrigée sous-estimerait la vraie moyenne de terrain et rendrait l'uniformité meilleure qu'elle ne l'est ; l'entrée Δpression existe spécifiquement pour contrer ce biais. Les valeurs à 1 ou au-dessus restent possibles (par exemple, l'estimation Δpression est trop faible, ou une course favorable en pente descendante). q<sub>dernier</sub>/q<sub>conception</sub> est un contrôle différent, non-uniformité, contre le débit nominal du fabricant – utile pour détecter un système globalement sur- ou sous-pressurisé, mais pas un substitut au chiffre d'uniformité, puisque le débit de conception/nominal n'a aucune relation nécessaire à la pression moyenne de fonctionnement réelle du système.
next_translated.english: Models one fixed inlet pressure (no pump curve), one test path only (not the full field), and a 2-parameter emitter curve (set the exponent near 0 to approximate a pressure-compensating emitter). Two different ratios are reported, deliberately kept separate: q<sub>last</sub>/q<sub>avg,field</sub> is a uniformity check, shaped like textbook low-quarter Distribution Uniformity (low-group average ÷ population mean) but computed from the test lateral’s own modeled emitters, corrected by an entered Δpressure estimate rather than a full-field statistical sample — the test lateral is deliberately the presumed worst case, so its raw, uncorrected average would understate the true field average and make uniformity look better than it is; the Δpressure input exists specifically to counter that bias. Values at or above 1 are still possible (e.g. the Δpressure estimate is too small, or a favorable downhill run). q<sub>last</sub>/q<sub>design</sub> is a different, non-uniformity check against the manufacturer’s rated flow — useful for spotting an over- or under-pressured system overall, but not a substitute for the uniformity number, since the design/rated flow has no necessary relationship to the system’s actual mean operating pressure.

previous_translated.value: Le taux d'application et le débit de la zone/système utilisent le débit moyen estimé du goutteur sur le terrain (q<sub>moy,terrain</sub> – la propre moyenne de la rampe de test, corrigée par l'estimation Δpression saisie), pas un taux deviné : PR = q<sub>moy,terrain</sub> / A<sub>e</sub>, alimenté par la valeur modélisée corrigée. L'espacement et les comptes latéraux/goutteurs à l'échelle du système sont des entrées séparées ici car le cheminement de test modélise uniquement une branche au pire cas, pas chaque rampe du champ.
previous_translated.english: Application rate and system/zone flow use the estimated field-average emitter flow (q<sub>avg,field</sub> — the test lateral’s own average, corrected by the entered Δpressure estimate), not a guessed rate: PR = q<sub>avg,field</sub> / A<sub>e</sub>, fed by the corrected modeled value. Spacing and system-wide lateral/emitter counts are separate inputs here because the test path only models one worst-case branch, not every lateral in the field.
